text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 24 in history.
1360 - The Treaty of Calais was signed by Edward III of England and John II of France, allowing England to keep certain French territories.
1618 - Aurangzeb was born. Last of the great Mughal Emperors of India, he reigned from 1658-1707.
1632 - Dutch biologist and microscopist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek born. He was the first person to observe bacteria and made many medical discoveries concerning blood circulation.
1648 - The Treaty of Westphalia was signed between France and the Holy Roman Empire at Munster, finally ending the Thirty Years War.
1795 - Poland ceased to exist as an independent state when the Third Partition was negotiated between Russia, Prussia and Austria, dividing the remaining Polish territory between them.
1861 - The first U.S. transcontinental telegram was sent from San Francisco by the Chief Justice of California to U.S. President Abraham Lincoln in Washington.
1891 - Generalissimo Rafael Leonidas Trujillo Molina born. Dictator of the Dominican Republic from 1930 until his assassination on 31 May 1961.
1893 - Merian C Cooper born. U.S. adventurer, explorer and film director and producer. He co-directed "King Kong" in 1933 and co-produced the first cinerama presentation, "This Is Cinerama", in 1952.

1904 - Moss Hart born. U.S. playwright, director and screenwriter who collaborated with George S Kaufman on many successful plays including "The Man Who Came to Dinner" He also wrote the screenplay for many films including "A Star is Born".
1915 - Tito Gobbi born. Noted Italian baritone and a fine actor. He appeared opposite Maria Callas in his most famous role in Puccini's opera "Tosca".
1929 - Share prices collapsed as nearly 13 million shares changed hands in panic selling on the New York Stock Exchange in what became known as "Black Thursday".
1944 - In World War Two, the Japanese battleship "Musashi", one of the largest ever built, was sunk by U.S. planes during the Battle of Leyte Gulf.
1945 - Adopted by the San Francisco Conference in June 1945, the United Nations Charter formally came into force.
1945 - Vidkun Quisling, prime minister of Norway during the German occupation, was executed by firing squad in Oslo after being convicted of high treason.
1964 - Northern Rhodesia became independent as the Republic of Zambia with Kenneth Kaunda as president.
1980 - In Poland, the authorities granted recognition to new independent trade union "Solidarity".
1986 - Jordanian Nezar Hindawi was sentenced to 45 years' jail by a London court for trying to blow up an Israeli airliner.
1989 - U.S. television evangelist Jim Bakker was sentenced to 45 years in jail and fined $500,000 for swindling his followers.
1994 - For the first time in 25 years no British troops were on the streets of Londonderry in British-ruled Northern Ireland, as British and Irish government forces scaled back security measures.
